newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem seen signing airport sale decree Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Menem seen signing airport sale decree Thursday.

text.p: President Carlos Menem will likely sign a decree ordering the privatization of Argentina's main airports this week, Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez said Monday.
"The president will probably proceed to sign the decree opening the door for the privatization of airports on Thursday," the Menem aide told FM News radio.

Rodriguez said he expected Argentina's air terminals to be in private hands by August or early September. Eighteen national airports and another 17 to 18 provincial terminals will be privatized, including the two serving Buenos Aires.

The airports will be transfered to private hands through a concession rather than a sale because the law does not allow a sell-off when it is done by presidential decree rather than congressional law, he said.
Government officials will embark on road shows to ensure major international investors get to know the details. Rodriguez did not say how long the concessions would last.
"We, as all Argentines, hope that once this is under way we will have airports on a par with other transformations that have taken place in the country," he said.

The government originally planned last year to sell up to 59 airports, but Menem's government was unable to push the bill through a reluctant lower chamber of Congress and eventually settled for a scaled-down version of fewer terminals and concessions instead of sales.
However, the 36 privatizations mentioned by Rodriguez far exceeded the 25 estimated by the government as possible only last month.
More than 20 international companies have expressed interest in the privatizations, in which Union Bank of Switzerland is acting as advisor to the government.

Rodriguez said earlier plans to build an airport on an artificial island on the River Plate to replace both Ezeiza and Aeroparque terminals in Buenos Aires have not been scrapped but would now become a decision for the future concessionaires to take.
"If that project takes place, the Aeroparque lands will be turned into a park," he said.
Rodriguez's anouncements came four weeks after Menem signed another decree to privatize the postal service.
The president embarked on an ambitious privatization drive soon after first taking office in 1989, selling off everything from utilities to railroads, airlines, ports and highways.
The airports, along with the country's nuclear plants and hydroelectric dams, are some of the few remaining state-owned firms not yet handed over to private hands.
